name: B/5 Treaty Investor Visa

qualifying_event.description: A US citizen purchases or invests in at least 50% ownership of an active Israeli business that employs Israeli citizens (not solely foreign workers) and demonstrates sufficient economic contribution, applying for a B/5 visa via the Ministry of Interior. This route is available regardless of Jewish ancestry or Law of Return eligibility.
qualifying_event.evidence_hint: Proof of at least 50% business ownership; evidence the business employs Israelis and is profitable.

requirements.blocker_text: Available to US citizens only, under the US-Israel treaty basis for this visa category.
At least 50% ownership of an active Israeli business.
The business must employ Israeli citizens; it cannot employ only foreign workers.

outcome.duration_length: initial 2 years, renewable annually thereafter, extendable beyond 63 months (5 years) while the business remains active

sources.title: Decker, Pex, Levi Law Firm (Israeli immigration law firm) -- B/5 investor visa: US citizens only, 50%+ ownership of an active Israeli business employing Israeli citizens; initial 2-year validity, annual renewal, extendable beyond 63 months; spouses receive B/5-2 and children under 21 receive B/5-3 dependent visas with work/study rights but no access to public social services

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Israel). STATUS: DRAFT -- entirely tier-3 sourced (a specialized immigration law firm) after Israel's own gov.il/embassy pages on this specific visa were not reached in this pass. STRUCTURAL FINDING worth flagging prominently: this route is restricted to US CITIZENS ONLY, arising from a bilateral US-Israel treaty basis rather than a general investor-residence category open to any nationality -- unlike Jordan's, Vietnam's, or Latvia's investor routes, which are nationality-neutral. No general, nationality-neutral investor residence route was found for Israel in this pass; a non-US investor appears to need Law of Return eligibility (see il_citizenship_by_return.json) or another route entirely. leads_to_pr/leads_to_citizenship are both false since the source describes this as a renewable business-linked status, not a settlement pathway, and family members are explicitly barred from public social-service access even while resident -- disclosed as a real, sourced restriction rather than smoothed over.
